name: Nat Ganley
bio: Nat Ganley was a Detroit Communist Party leader and auto-union figure prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in 1954 of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Saul Wellman
bio: Saul Wellman was a Detroit Communist and World War II veteran prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in 1954 of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government and remained on bail pending appeal.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government
sentence: Convicted under the Smith Act; on bail pending appeal

name: Thomas Dennis
bio: Thomas Dennis was a Black Communist Party leader in Detroit prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in 1954 of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Phil Schatz
bio: Phil Schatz was a Detroit Communist prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in 1954 of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Anna Bary
bio: Anna Bary was a Denver Communist and Mexican-rights activist arrested under the Smith Act in August 1954 during the McCarthy era. She was jailed on bail set between $25,000 and $40,000, with trial set for January 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Lewis Johnson
bio: Lewis Johnson was a Denver Communist arrested under the Smith Act in August 1954 during the McCarthy era. He was jailed on bail set between $15,000 and $30,000, with trial set for January 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Harold Zepelin
bio: Harold Zepelin was a Denver-born Communist arrested under the Smith Act in August 1954 during the McCarthy era. He was jailed for roughly 114 days, with trial set for January 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Maia Scherrer
bio: Maia Scherrer was a Denver Communist and secretary of the Colorado defense committee, arrested under the Smith Act in August 1954 during the McCarthy era. She was released on $5,000 bail, with trial set for January 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Joseph Scherrer
bio: Joseph Scherrer was a Denver Communist arrested under the Smith Act in August 1954 during the McCarthy era. He was released on $5,000 bail, with trial set for January 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Patricia Blau
bio: Patricia Blau was a Denver Communist arrested under the Smith Act in August 1954 during the McCarthy era. She was also tried, and acquitted, of harboring fugitive Robert Thompson.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government
convicted: Indicted 1954; acquitted of separate charge of harboring fugitive Robert Thompson

name: Claude Lightfoot
bio: Claude Lightfoot was a prominent Black Communist Party leader in Chicago arrested in 1954 under the Smith Act's membership clause during the McCarthy era. He faced up to 10 years in prison, with trial set for January 1955.
charges: Smith Act 'membership clause' — being a member of the Communist Party
sentence: Faced up to 10 years in prison

name: Martha Stone Asher
bio: Martha Stone Asher was a New Jersey Communist seized from the Party's underground in 1954 during the McCarthy era. She was charged under the Smith Act's membership clause.
charges: Smith Act membership clause
sentence: Charged under the Smith Act membership clause

name: Albert Blumberg
bio: Albert Blumberg was a Maryland-District of Columbia Communist Party leader arrested in 1954 under the Smith Act's membership clause during the McCarthy era. He was held on $40,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act membership clause

name: Carl Ross
bio: Carl Ross was a Communist arrested in August 1953 and tried in San Francisco for sheltering Smith Act fugitives Robert Thompson and Sidney Stein during the McCarthy era. He was convicted of harboring in April 1954.
charges: Harboring Communist Smith Act fugitives

name: Shirley Kremen
bio: Shirley Kremen was a student tried in San Francisco for sheltering Smith Act fugitives Robert Thompson and Sidney Stein during the McCarthy era. She was convicted of harboring in April 1954 and sentenced to one year.
charges: Harboring Communist Smith Act fugitives

name: Sam Coleman
bio: Sam Coleman was a Communist Party official tried in San Francisco for sheltering Smith Act fugitives Robert Thompson and Sidney Stein during the McCarthy era. He was convicted of harboring in April 1954 and sentenced to three years.
charges: Harboring Communist Smith Act fugitives

name: Sidney Stein
bio: Sidney Stein was a Smith Act fugitive who was being harbored and who was under Smith Act indictment during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in April 1954 in connection with the San Francisco harboring case.
charges: Smith Act (fugitive) and the conduct underlying the SF harboring case
sentence: Convicted in connection with the harboring case

name: Joseph Dimow
bio: Joseph Dimow was a Connecticut Communist who held local party offices in the late 1940s and served on the party's state committee in 1953–54. He was one of the New Haven Smith Act defendants indicted and tried in 1954 during the McCarthy era for conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government; the convictions were reversed by the Second Circuit in United States v. Silverman (1957).
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government
convicted: Indicted and tried 1954; conviction reversed on appeal (1957)
sentence: Convicted under the Smith Act; reversed in United States v. Silverman

name: Jacob Goldring
bio: Jacob Goldring was a Connecticut Communist and member of the party's state committee through the late 1940s and early 1950s. He was one of the New Haven Smith Act defendants indicted and tried in 1954 during the McCarthy era for conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government; the convictions were reversed by the Second Circuit in United States v. Silverman (1957).
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government
convicted: Indicted and tried 1954; conviction reversed on appeal (1957)
sentence: Convicted under the Smith Act; reversed in United States v. Silverman

name: Robert Champion Ekins
bio: Robert Champion Ekins was the Communist Party's Connecticut state secretary in the early 1950s. He was one of the New Haven Smith Act defendants indicted and tried in 1954 during the McCarthy era for conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government; the convictions were reversed by the Second Circuit in United States v. Silverman (1957).
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government
convicted: Indicted and tried 1954; conviction reversed on appeal (1957)
sentence: Convicted under the Smith Act; reversed in United States v. Silverman

name: Simon Silverman
bio: Simon Silverman (also known as Sid Taylor) was a Connecticut Communist Party organizer and the lead defendant in the New Haven Smith Act case. Indicted and tried in 1954 during the McCarthy era for conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government, his conviction was reversed by the Second Circuit in United States v. Silverman (248 F.2d 671, 1957).
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government
convicted: Indicted and tried 1954; conviction reversed on appeal (1957)
sentence: Convicted under the Smith Act; reversed in United States v. Silverman

name: Frank Collier
bio: Frank Collier was a Boston Communist arrested in 1954 in the New England roundup of Smith Act defendants during the McCarthy era. He was charged with conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
charges: Smith Act — conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government

name: Albert Shadowitz
bio: Albert Shadowitz was an engineer who refused to answer Senator McCarthy's questions on the advice of Albert Einstein during the McCarthy era. He was cited and indicted in 1954 for contempt of Congress.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee

name: Abraham Unger
bio: Abraham Unger was a New York attorney who refused to answer Senator McCarthy's questions during the McCarthy era. He was cited and indicted in 1954 for contempt of Congress.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee

name: Goldie Watson
bio: Goldie Watson was a Black former Philadelphia teacher cited in 1954 for refusing, on First and Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee during the McCarthy era. She was cited for contempt of Congress.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee

name: Wilbur Maheney
bio: Wilbur Maheney was a Philadelphian who admitted past Communist Party membership but refused to name others before a Congressional committee during the McCarthy era. He was cited in 1954 for contempt of Congress.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee

name: Emanuel Fried
bio: Emanuel Fried was a Buffalo union leader who challenged a House Un-American Activities Committee subcommittee during the McCarthy era. He was cited for contempt of Congress for refusing, on First and Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer the committee.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee

name: H. Chandler Davis
bio: H. Chandler Davis was a University of Michigan mathematics instructor who invoked the Fifth Amendment before a Congressional committee during the McCarthy era. He faced prosecution for contempt of Congress.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee
sentence: Faced prosecution for contempt of Congress

name: William Ullman
bio: William Ullman, named by Elizabeth Bentley, was the first test of the Brownell immunity law during the McCarthy era. He faced contempt of Congress for refusing, on First and Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee

name: Paul Sweezy
bio: Paul Sweezy was editor of the Monthly Review who was jailed and cited for refusing the New Hampshire attorney-general's questions about a university lecture during the McCarthy era. His case went on appeal and was later decided as Sweezy v. New Hampshire.
charges: Contempt of Congress — for refusing, on First/Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Congressional committee
sentence: Jailed and cited; case on appeal (later Sweezy v. New Hampshire)
